paragraphs.text: A loose [red tea](red:definition) from Taiwan, made in 2023. Red tea is the tea English calls black; its Chinese name follows the colour of the brewed cup rather than the dark dry leaf. Taiwan's own red tea goes back to [the Japanese period, at Yuchi near Sun Moon Lake](red:history).

The leaf is [withered until soft, then rolled](red:making) so its juices and enzymes meet. It is left to oxidise fully until it turns from green to reddish brown, and hot air then stops the change and keeps the tea stable.

At three years it sits at the far edge of what a red tea keeps. The style [has no tradition of ageing](red:ageing): sealed, it holds its quality for a year and a half to three years, so this is a tea for drinking now rather than keeping.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
